Babhruvāhana
------------------------------------------
When अर्जुन, the Pāṇḍava hero, was on a tour, as penance, he went to the kingdom of Citravāhana, ruling at Maṇalūr. The king offered his daughter चित्राङ्गदा in मर्रिअगे to him. Babhru-वाहन was the son born to them. He grew up into a great warrior worthy of his ड़थेर्.
After the कुरुक्षेत्र war, when युधिष्ठिर decided to perform the Aśva-medha sacrifice, अर्जुन escorted the sacri-ficial horse through various kingdoms. The horse was caught by बभ्रुवाहन; and in the ensuing fight अर्जुन was killed by him, but was revived by Ulūpī, another wife of अर्जुन, by placing the Sañjīvaka-मणि, a precious stone capable of reviving dead persons, on his chest.
Babhruvāhana attended the Aśva-medha sacrifice at हस्तिनापुर.
See also CITRĀṄGADĀ and ULŪPĪ.

Bābhravya
(‘descendant of Babhru’)
------------------------------------------
Being a patronymic name it represents anyone who is a descendant of the sage Babhru. The sage Girija of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the sage शङ्ख of Jaiminīya Upaniṣad Brāhmaṇa were Bābhravyas.
The sage Gālava, mentioned in the Mahābhārata, was also a बाभ्रव्य. He was a great योगि and had organized the science of euphony of the वेदस् (called शिक्षा).
The Skāndapurāṇa mentions a बाभ्रव्य. अर्जुन, the Pāṇḍava hero, during his पिल्ग्रिमगे, met बाभ्रव्य and heard from him about the greatness of the sage नारद.
One बाभ्रव्य is said to have produced a condensed version of काम-śāstra (the Science of Erotics), originally written by श्वेतकेतु.
